verdicts.quote: OAuth authentication is still required to connect
verdicts.reason: Otter’s official MCP server uses an OAuth sign-in/consent flow; for a multi-tenant agent, MCP OAuth is the primary path even though the REST API itself uses bearer tokens. ([help.otter.ai](https://help.otter.ai/hc/en-us/articles/35287607569687-Otter-MCP-Server))

verdicts.quote: Yes, Otter offers a public API for Enterprise customers. To get started, contact your Otter account manager to enable access.
verdicts.reason: Not self-serve/free: the Public API is Enterprise-only and must be enabled by an account manager. ([help.otter.ai](https://help.otter.ai/hc/en-us/articles/4412365535895-Does-Otter-offer-an-open-API?utm_source=openai))

verdicts.quote: provides programmatic access to retrieve channels, conversations, transcripts, audio, action items, insights, outlines, and workspace details
verdicts.reason: Multiple core resources/endpoints are covered, but it’s not the entire product surface, which fits “moderate.” ([help.otter.ai](https://help.otter.ai/hc/en-us/articles/36130822688279-Otter-ai-Public-API))
Vendor-operated, documented MCP server and setup instructions confirm it’s an official MCP. ([help.otter.ai](https://help.otter.ai/hc/en-us/articles/35287607569687-Otter-MCP-Server))

Buildable now via the official MCP server (OAuth, documented JSON config), but the richer REST API/Webhooks are Enterprise-gated—so shipping an agent is feasible with caveats. ([otter.ai](https://otter.ai/pricing?geo=US))
